source.name: Bengaluru public mobility studies and corridor traffic surveys
source.note: Peak timing is shown only where a published survey/study provides usable local timing evidence. No zone-specific travel-time multiplier is inferred.

orr-east.message: The eastern ORR contains several documented high-volume junctions. Available corridor surveys put the critical morning period around 9–10 AM and evening around 5:30–6:30 PM.

whitefield.message: Whitefield approaches include high-volume eastern junctions. Local peak timing evidence is less complete, so the eastern ORR timing is used as a cautious proxy rather than a separate travel-time curve.

south-east.message: Central Silk Board is among Bengaluru's most heavily loaded documented junctions. Corridor counts around Iblur/Silk Board show a strong morning peak around 9–10 AM and evening peak around 5:30–6:30 PM.

north-airport.message: Hebbal and nearby northern corridors have strong published peak-hour evidence. Studies place the morning peak broadly around 9–11 AM and evening around 5–7 PM, with individual northern count points peaking between 9:00 and 11:15 AM.

central.message: Current public evidence is not strong enough to assign a separate Central Bengaluru peak shape, so the Bengaluru-wide TomTom timing curve is used.

south.message: Public counts confirm busy South Bengaluru junctions, but the current evidence is not strong enough to assign a distinct local peak-time curve. The citywide timing curve is used.

west.message: A Goragunte Palya traffic study observed a broad morning congestion period from about 7:45–10:40 AM and evening from about 5:30–8:30 PM.
